## A. Construct the point before fixing the second trace — lead direction

**Saved work sought:** replace a search for the first nontrivial rational point

by its elliptic group law. This is a primitive proposal, not a root-supply claim.
It changes which object is selected first; it does not assume a point oracle.

Delta=s^2-4t^2 positive nonsquare, and s=5R mod N. In W004, the second
trace s_j was fixed before searching
W^2=f(X)*f(s_j-X). Set b=s_j-s, z=X-s_j/2 and
a=f(s_j/2), c=2a-b^2. Direct expansion gives

    W^2=z^4+c*z^2+a^2,
    c+2a=-Delta, c-2a=-b^2.

The explicit cubic is

    E_b: y^2=x*(x+b^2)*(x+Delta),
    x=2*(W+z^2)+c, y=2*z*x,

The explicit section genuinely removes the first rational-point search:
P=(4t^2,2tsw) on y^2=x(x+b^2)(x+Delta), with
b=t(r-1/r), w=t(r+1/r), Delta=s^2-4t^2. Whether it is generically

Write d_+=s+2t and d_-=s-2t. The inverse quartic coordinates factor as

    X=(r+1)*(d_+*r+d_-)/(4r),
    Y=s_j-X=(r-1)*(d_+-d_-*r)/(4r).

Thus finding u^2=X and v^2=Y is the simultaneous cover

    A^2=r*(r+1)*(d_+*r+d_-),    A=2r*u,
    B^2=r*(r-1)*(d_+-d_-*r),    B=2r*v.

For s>2t>0, its six distinct branch places are
0, infinity, -1, -d_-/d_+, 1, d_+/d_-. The square classes are
independent (their simple zeros differ). At 0 and infinity the two
extensions ramify together with inertia 2, not 4 over an algebraic closure.
The degree-four cover has 2g-2=-8+6*2=4, hence genus 3.
This is a smaller geometric problem than the fixed-trace genus-7 norm
cover, but not a rational parametrization or efficient point algorithm.
The second trace now varies, so this is not a contradiction of W004.

It has three genus-one quotients: the A curve, the B curve, and

    C^2=(r^2-1)*(d_+*r+d_-)*(d_+-d_-*r),    C=A*B/r.

The first two are isomorphic by r -> -1/r and the ordinate scaling r^2:
F_A(-1/r)=F_B(r)/r^4. This extra structure is a concrete possible
replacement for unstructured high-genus searching, not a granted solver.
Using a Jacobian decomposition requires its maps, rational-point recovery,
height bounds and useful-input success law to be paid.

## The immediate local obstruction

On the intended branch r=1 mod N, one has X=s=5R mod N and Y=0 mod N.
For an unknown prime p|N with 5 nonsquare mod p, no rational square u^2=X
with p-integral u can exist. This obstruction holds regardless of how many
elliptic additions are advertised for the displayed section family.

More strongly, for the literal choice r=1+N/K with K=N*s^2+1, at every
odd prime p|N the second factor d_+-d_-*r equals 4t modulo p and is a
unit. Since 4r is a unit,

    v_p(Y)=v_p(r-1)=v_p(N).

Any odd exponent in N therefore prevents Y from being a rational square.
This kills the literal section's square lift on every squarefree composite.
It is an exact valuation obstruction, not a finite failure count.

**A genuine modification, not an automatic repair:** replacing r-1 by
t*N^2/K^2 gives

    Y=(t*N/K)^2 *
      (1-(s-2t)*N^2/(4K^2))/(1+t*N^2/K^2).

The displayed factor has unit reduction 1 and even N-adic valuation, so
the immediate parity obstruction disappears. It still has to be a rational
square exactly, with K checked for units and for the original interval.
Its being a square modulo N is not sufficient. X still reduces to 5R,
so the nonsquare-5 obstruction remains.

Changing the original modular coefficients to t=cR,
s=(1+c^2)R with rational c and 1+c^2=a^2 (known rational a)
removes the nonsquare constant. But on this section u^2=X then gives
(u/a)^2=R modulo N immediately. The lift is now explicitly the desired
modular-root computation, not a free auxiliary task. Choose unit
denominators and nonzero distinct modular roots before using this observation.

both its result and this response. No experiment or numerical search ran.

The reflection proposal has a specific likely defect: its useful quaternion
gcd is already visible in a scalar dot-product gcd. A materially different
case occurs when the scalar test gives the full modulus at every prime, but
left versus right orientation differs. Exact orthogonality forces precisely
that scalar degeneracy. It deserves a direct extraction criterion.

## Proposed extraction lemma, including all odd prime powers

Let A,B be integer-coordinate quaternions, with

    Norm(A)=Norm(B)=N odd, and <A,B>=0.

Identify their coordinate columns with a,b. Put

    V=B*conjugate(A), W=conjugate(A)*B,
    g_V=gcd(N,V_i,V_j,V_k), g_W=gcd(N,W_i,W_j,W_k).

V and W are pure and each has norm N^2. The proposed identity is

    L_V R_W = N^2 I_4 - 2N*(a*a^T+b*b^T),

where L_V,R_W mean real left/right multiplication on quaternions.

Proof: these two commuting skew-symmetric multiplication matrices have
symmetric product. That product has square N^4 I, has eigenvalue -N^2
on A and B, and has trace zero. Its other two eigenvalues are therefore
+N^2. Since A,B are orthogonal with squared length N, the displayed
orthogonal-projector formula follows. Trace zero also follows directly from
trace(L_u R_v)=4 Re(u)Re(v).

For e_i,e_j in {i,j,k}, the nine matrices L_(e_i) R_(e_j) are pairwise
orthogonal for the Frobenius inner product, each with squared norm 4.
Taking their inner product with the displayed identity shows

    N divides 4*V_i*W_j, hence N divides V_i*W_j since N is odd.

At each p^e dividing N, minimum coordinate valuations consequently give
v_p(g_V)+v_p(g_W)>=e. Thus N divides g_V*g_W, without a squarefree
assumption or knowledge of the primes in the algorithm.

If g_V=N, then V=N*u with u a pure integer quaternion of norm 1,
so u is one of +/-i,+/-j,+/-k and B=u*A.
If g_V=1, then g_W=N, giving B=A*u for one of the same six units.
Therefore any orthogonal B of equal norm that avoids the at most twelve
vectors u*A and A*u necessarily gives **1<g_V<N**.

This is a deterministic polynomial-bit extraction from a supplied pair,
not a way to obtain the pair. No quaternion gcd implementation is needed:
two products, integer gcds, and checking the norm/orthogonality suffice.
All input coordinates have O(log N) bits. The obvious twelve exceptions
can be listed and compared at polynomial cost. Some exceptions themselves
might yield other gcd information; the sufficient criterion does not claim
they all fail.

## An actual finite generator, and why its current cost is uncompetitive

Given a primitive A, compute a rank-three integer basis H for
L={z in Z^4: <A,z>=0} by extended gcd/Hermite reduction. Its covolume
is sqrt(N). Reduce H if desired, charging reduction, and put G=H^T H.

For every coordinate t_i of a vector Ht of squared length N, exact
Cauchy-Schwarz gives

    |t_i| <= floor(sqrt(N*(G^(-1))_ii)) = B_i.

Choose the two smallest B_i, enumerate their two integer coordinates,
and solve the remaining integer quadratic equation exactly using its
discriminant and divisibility conditions. For every solution, reconstruct B,
reject the twelve exceptions, and use the extraction lemma. This is an
explicit search, including finite termination and output checking. Its
cost is bounded by

    C_A + C_basis + O((2B_1+1)*(2B_2+1)*poly(log N)),

where C_A includes obtaining A and widths of any chosen basis algorithm
must be bounded. No fast all-input sampler or favorable basis shape is
granted. If there is no nonexceptional pair, report failure at that scope.

In an isotropic geometry with basis lengths about N^(1/6), these coordinate
bounds are about N^(1/3), so the two-coordinate scan is about N^(2/3).
That is a shape diagnostic, not a proved average or worst-case count.
It already gives no reason to expect a factoring improvement. LLL finds
short vectors in the ball; it does not directly find an exact vector on the
specified sphere or remove the twelve exceptional answers.

The next computation to change is now precise: solve the exact ternary
quadratic equation t^T G t=N while excluding those known points, with
less total work than the appropriate factoring comparator. A proposed
binary-slice prime search must pay for the slice discriminant, class
membership, prime generation and failed slices. Calling fixed dimension
or a short lattice basis a fast exact-shell solver is invalid.

## The rational-rotation version exposes the same integral constraint

Another explicit representation asks for a pure integer quaternion C with

    Norm(C)=N^2, C*A=0 mod N,

and sets B=C*A/N. Then B is integral, orthogonal to A and has norm N.
The congruence lattice can be constructed by integer linear algebra;
the norm equation remains. It is a denominator-N transformation, so it
changes the failed unit-denominator reflection representation materially.
It does not grant division by N in modular arithmetic.

A shorter rational rotation with a denominator coprime to N preserves the
same local orientation at every prime. Merely changing its rational
parameter cannot produce the mixed orientation needed here. A denominator
with proper gcd already factors N; full-modulus denominators require the
paid integral constraint above.

## Primary prior art checked; no novelty assertion

This general research route is already present in
[Machiavelo–Rocadas, Connections between the arithmetic and the geometry of
Lipschitz integers](https://cmup.fc.up.pt/main/sites/default/files/publications/Quaternions_AM_LR.pdf).
Its introduction explicitly motivates orthogonal four-square pairs for
factoring. Lemma 4.2 supplies an orthogonal-lattice basis; Theorems 4.3–4.4
show why natural vector-product constructions preserve left/right multiples.
Thus an unmodified cross-product generator is not a new escape.

[Kiss–Kutas, Cubes of integral vectors in dimension four](https://ewkiss.web.elte.hu/wp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2014/11/Int4vec9.pdf),
Lemma 3.3 and Theorem 3.5, classify local common divisors and express an
orthogonal tuple as gamma*epsilon_i*delta. This supports the need to charge
the factor-bearing decomposition; it is not a polynomial-time construction
from an unfactored N.

Read scope: the former's introduction, Lemma 4.2, Theorems 4.3–4.4 and final
remarks; the latter's Lemmas 3.1–3.4 and Theorem 3.5, including the displayed
proofs. PDF conjugation marks require visual inspection; the retained
extraction lemma above is independently derived rather than trusting text
extraction with missing bars. PDFs and hashes are in W005-parent-sources.
No claim of a complete literature survey or novel reduction follows.

ORIGINAL NEW MECHANISM, FINDINGS AND UNRESOLVED OBJECTIONS:
# W005 — blinded Norm2 from the outer square, with an explicit sampler

Date: 2026-10-08. **PROVISIONAL parent mechanism; independent review required.**
This changes the joint factoring wrapper, not the old standalone N,R-only
Norm2 contract. No assertion of a new best factoring bound or novelty.
It was developed while the other T3 reviews ran.

## Computation removed

The old reference finds u^2+v^2=5R mod N by two O(N)-length lists.
But the outer trial itself selected a unit x and R=x^2 mod N. It knows
the easy representation (x,2x). Passing this inward unchanged exposes the
root and invalidates the useful-root probability proof.

The proposal is to randomize that representation with an EXACTLY uniform
norm-one rotation, cheaply. The resulting auxiliary representation should be
independent of which root x in the R fiber was used. This supplies a new
joint sampler for factoring, not a free root or an N,R-only Norm2 algorithm.

## Actual algorithm

Assume gcd(N,30)=1, x a unit, R=x^2 mod N, and n=bitlength(N).

1. Sample a,b independently uniformly from {0,...,N-1}, using separately
   rejected n-bit words. Set h=a^2+b^2 mod N and d=gcd(h,N).
2. If 1<d<N, return the verified factor. If d=N, retry within the cap.
3. If d=1, compute h^(-1) mod N and

       c=(a^2-b^2)/h,  e=2ab/h,
       u=x*(c-2e),     v=x*(e+2c)     mod N.

   Return canonical u,v only, along with N,R, to the inner field/packet
   procedure. Do not pass x,a,b,c,e or their sampler tape to that procedure.

Then c^2+e^2=1 and u^2+v^2=5R mod N. This uses a constant number
of O(n)-bit modular operations per pair. Rejecting a or b outside range is
charged. For a fixed worst-case cap, use B=2*(n+1)^3 pair attempts and
finite caps on each raw-word rejection as specified below. A cap stop is a
failure, not a successful norm certificate.

For a simpler expected-cost variant, uniform sampling may use unbounded
rejection; the expected number of n-bit words per coordinate is <2.
The finite-raw-bit variant can allocate 2*(n+1) raw draws per coordinate
per pair, abandoning that pair if either coordinate never enters [0,N).
Conditional on entry, the coordinates remain exactly uniform. These
abandonments belong in the failure probability and cost.

The inner routine may depend on N,R,u,v and independent randomness, including
arbitrary adaptive filters of those values. The outer routine uses x only
to compare against a returned root. This interface restriction is substantive.

## Proposed exact independence proof

Work in S=(Z/NZ)[i], i^2=-1, with conjugation and norm. The accepted pair
xi=a+ib is uniform among units of S. Its rotation is xi/conjugate(xi).

The kernel of xi -> xi/conjugate(xi) is exactly the scalar units: if a
unit equals its conjugate, 2 invertible forces its i coefficient to zero.
Thus each image fiber has phi(N) members.

Surjectivity onto every c+ie with c^2+e^2=1 follows locally modulo p^k.
If 1+c is a unit, choose xi=(1+c)+ie, with norm 2(1+c).
Otherwise 1-c is a unit, and xi=e+i(1-c), with norm 2(1-c).
Both give the desired rotation. CRT proves existence globally; factors
are used only in this proof, never by the sampler. Hence the rotation is
uniform in the norm-one group, including repeated prime powers.

The element z_0=x(1+2i) has unit norm 5R. Multiplication by norm-one
elements acts freely and transitively on all z=u+iv of norm 5R:
the unique multiplier is z/z_0. Consequently the returned certificate is
uniform on that set for every fixed x in the root fiber. Its distribution
is exactly independent of x conditional on N,R.

Earlier rejected pairs, their count, and the factor/accepted/failure branch
depend on N and sampler randomness, not x. Even a bounded stopping rule
of the stated kind preserves the conditional uniform certificate law.
The final rotation tape must remain unavailable to the inner routine:
it would allow inversion back to x. No secrecy from the mathematical
algorithm or the outer verifier is assumed; this is a data-dependence
condition for the root returned by the inner subroutine.

## Paid sampling bound

For an odd p, the fraction of pairs with a^2+b^2 nonzero mod p is
(1-1/p)^2 if -1 is a square, and 1-1/p^2 otherwise. Prime-power lifts
have the same fraction. Therefore the unit-pair probability is at least

    product_(p|N) (1-1/p)^2 = (phi(N)/N)^2 >= 1/(n+1)^2.

For the last bound, order the r distinct primes increasingly and use
p_j>=j+1, giving product(1-1/p_j)>=1/(r+1), with r<=n.
No analytic prime theorem, factoring routine, smoothness or unproved
sampler theorem is used.

Expected pair count until a factor or a certificate is therefore polynomial
in n. With finite raw-word caps, the chance both coordinates are sampled
is at least (1-2^(-2(n+1)))^2, a constant near one; price this factor explicitly
rather than silently retaining the untruncated bound. The stated pair and
raw-word caps give worst-case polynomial work, while any exhaustion stays
in the failure denominator. Exact tail constants are for the independent
review; a near-one certificate probability is not necessary for the
old-gcd complete upper bound below.

## What changes in the factoring wrapper

Conditional on N,R and the complete INNER transcript (which excludes the
blinding tape), x should remain uniform on its 2^r roots, even with
repeated odd prime powers. Hence any inner root y splits with conditional
probability 1-2/2^r, as in the old reduction. Auxiliary norm certificates
are permitted because they are independent of that hidden root choice.

W004's algebra accepts any verified norm representation. Its two-field
selector and M=n^2 scans otherwise have polynomial per-trial bit work.
Replacing the Norm2 lists by the capped sampler therefore proposes a
polynomial-cost trial, under a CHANGED certificate distribution. It does
not inherit any unproved target-supply law from the old deterministic
representation. Field/packet failures, sampler exhaustion, raw words x>=N,
and x=0 remain failures; all proper gcds remain checked successes.

Even using only the original nonunit-x success mass >=1/(4sqrt(N)),
a polynomial-cost trial gives a conservative complete expected
O(sqrt(N_0)*poly(log N_0)) wrapper, after paid preprocessing and recursion.
This would improve the OLD W004 reference upper bound
O(N_0^(3/2)*poly(log N_0)), but does not improve trial division or the
established general factoring state of the art.

The actual new computational claim to validate is the cheap, root-choice-
independent auxiliary sampler. It removes a concrete setup cost and permits
cheap sampling/filtering of field constructions; it does not prove useful
packet supply. A finite distribution check can falsify implementation
mistakes, while the uniformity and full cost need the symbolic argument.

- (z,W)=(0,−a) maps to (−b²,0).

For the second infinity, x=b²Delta/(4z²)+O(z⁻⁴) verifies the extension.
Thus these four points generate exactly E_b[2], with the first infinity
chosen as origin. They cannot generate a new point. This says nothing about
the full Mordell–Weil group. Here a≠0 follows from b²≠Delta.

## 3. The section — valid and generically infinite order

For b=t(r−r⁻¹), w=t(r+r⁻¹), P=(4t²,2tsw), the three cubic factors at P
are (2t)²,w²,s². Hence P lies on E_b; its ordinate is nonzero for real
nonzero r under these hypotheses. Exclude r=±1 and singular fibers.
The inverse formulas in the brief, including their factorizations, are correct.
For r>1, X>0, and Y>0 exactly when 1<r<d_+/d_−, where d_±=s±2t.
At either endpoint Y=0. Positivity is only a necessary lift condition.

**Symbolic order proof, not a numerical specialization.** Fix any rational
s>2t>0 and consider the local parameter r−1 over Q. At r=1 the cubic has
split multiplicative reduction after adjoining k=sqrt(Delta):

    y²=x²(x+Delta),   P_0=(4t²,4t²s),   q(P_0)=y/x=s.

P_0 is smooth. On the smooth nodal group use lambda=(q+k)/(q−k).
Its value at P_0 is (s+k)/(s−k)>1 in the real embedding with k>0.
It therefore has infinite multiplicative order. Specialization on the smooth
group is a homomorphism, so a torsion section would specialize to torsion,
a contradiction. This proves P has infinite order over Q(r), and also over
the generic Q(s,t,r). This proof uses a symbolic singular fiber, not a single
numerically tested smooth curve. The smooth-model group fact is documented in
[Lichtenstein §§4.1.7–4.3.2](https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~conrad/mordellsem/Notes/L11.pdf).

**Saved computation:** a rational norm point is produced by a fixed number of
rational operations after choosing the new trace. For K=Ns²+1 its height is
O(log N+h(s)+h(t)); construction and checks have polynomial bit cost at that
width. K and K+N are both 1 modulo N, so the claimed unit conditions on
r=(K+N)/K hold. The literal interval check reduces to
N/(Ns²+1)<4t/(s−2t), valid for the inherited integer s>2t≥4.
This does not find a point on the previously fixed second-trace curve.
Generic infinite order establishes a genuine section, not useful rational
square lifts or a bit-cost bound for its specialized multiples. Exact rational
scalar arithmetic must pay growing numerator/denominator lengths.
Retaining W004's reference first-field setup still pays O(N n²) time and
O(N n) working bits for its two-list Norm2, n=bitlength(N). These new
formulae do not remove that acquisition cost or replace its output law.

## 4. Intrinsic bad reduction, and a stronger computational identification

The proposed invariants are correct:

    c4=16(b⁴−b²Delta+Delta²),
    D_E=16 b⁴Delta²(b²−Delta)².

For p|N, b∈p A_N and Delta≡9R² is a unit. Thus c4 is a unit,
v_p(D_E)=4v_p(b)>0, and v_p(j)=−4v_p(b)<0. The equation is minimal
at p: a nonminimal integral rescaling would make v_p(c4)≥4. In particular
this is intrinsic split multiplicative bad reduction, not a removable defect
of the displayed model. A good integral model would have integral j.

Modulo p the node is (0,0), with tangent lines y=±kappa x, kappa=3R.
For its normalization,

    x=q²−kappa²,  y=q(q²−kappa²),
    lambda=(q+kappa)/(q−kappa),
    x=4kappa² lambda/(lambda−1)².

Exclude q=±kappa, the two branches over the node; q=infinity gives O and
lambda=1. This identifies the smooth group with F_p^*. To check the law
directly, a line y=m x+n cuts parameters satisfying
(q−m)(q²−kappa²)−n=0. Evaluating at ±kappa shows the product of their
lambdas is one. Negating y inverts lambda, exactly the chord-and-tangent law.

**Stronger consequence:** on every intended r≡1 branch, q(P)≡s≡5R,
so lambda(P)=4. Therefore lambda([k]P)=4^k. On finite charts with
4^k−1 nonzero modulo p, the quartic inverse gives

    X_k/R=(4·4^k−1)/(4^k−1),
    Y_k/R=(4^k−4)/(4^k−1).                            (1)

For scalar M, [M]P reduces to O exactly when 4^M≡1 (mod p).
This primewise detection is available directly through gcd(4^M−1,N):
binary exponentiation costs O(log M) modular multiplications, plus a gcd,
with O(log N)-bit residues. This replaces the rational-curve computation
for that detector. It is the p−1 mechanism at base 4, not random elliptic
orders; gcd=N still needs the ordinary proper-factor recovery analysis.
Intermediate affine denominators can detect additional coincidences, but
their smooth-group conditions likewise have explicit multiplicative images.
No equality of all possible denominator valuations is asserted. Points on
other components or reducing to the node are outside this smooth analysis.

This also **corrects the scope** of the parent's nonsquare-5 warning: X≡5R,
Y≡0 holds for the displayed section P(r), not every [k]P. Formula (1) is
the required replacement test for its multiples. For example, as a symbolic
scalar identity, k=3 gives X_3/R=85/21 and Y_3/R=20/21; their square
conditions involve the classes 17 and 105. They do not force the class 5
to be square: in Q(sqrt(17),sqrt(105)) both are squares and 5 is not.
This is a square-class counterexample to that algebraic implication, not
a finite-field numerical test or a claim of useful prime/input supply.

## 5. Simultaneous cover and quotient symmetry — recommend acceptance

The equations A²=F_A(r)=r(r+1)(d_+r+d_−),
B²=F_B(r)=r(r−1)(d_+−d_−r), with A=2ru and B=2rv, are exact.
For s>2t>0 their six branch places are exactly those listed by the parent.
Each radicand has a simple zero absent from the other, proving independence
in the geometric function field. At 0 and infinity their ratio is a local
unit and hence a square over the algebraically closed residue field, so
the inertia group there has order two. All six places contribute two;
Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g−2=−8+12=4, hence g=3.

The three sign quotients are the two cubics and

    C²=(r²−1)(d_+r+d_−)(d_+−d_−r),  C=AB/r.

Each has four distinct branch points and a rational branch point, hence is
an elliptic curve after an origin is chosen. The identity
F_A(−1/r)=F_B(r)/r⁴ is correct. On the full cover it extends to the
involution (r,A,B)↦(−1/r,B/r²,A/r²); on u,v it sends (u,v) to (−v,−u).
It interchanges the two tests; it does not remove either. The three quotient
pullbacks give the usual isogeny from their product to the genus-three
Jacobian (their distinct sign eigenspaces exhaust the three differentials).
An isogeny of Jacobians is not a rational-point parametrization of the cover.

A precise partial alternative is to generate a point (r,A) on the first
quotient and test F_B(r) for a rational square. That removes the first test,
but no nontrivial seed, finite-index generators, height bound or success law
for this quotient has been supplied. Its visible branch points alone are
two-torsion. A bounded rational-r scan with numerator/denominator ≤H costs
O(H² poly(log N+log H+h(s))) for the two tests; no useful cap is proved.
The materially different fixed-u operation in §7 removes both tests instead.

## 6. Local obstruction, repair, and the root circularity

For any p|N and r≡1, X is the unit 5R modulo p. A rational u satisfying
u²=X is automatically p-integral (indeed a unit), so nonsquare 5 excludes
such u. This is not merely a restriction imposed by a chosen denominator
convention. For the literal K=Ns²+1, r=1+N/K,

    v_p(Y)=v_p(r−1)+v_p(d_+−d_−r)−v_p(4r)=v_p(N),

because d_+−d_−r≡4t is a unit. An odd exponent of any prime in N
therefore rules out a rational v. In particular every inherited squarefree
composite fails this literal lift. Squareful N with all exponents even is
not thereby successful; rational squareness is global.

The proposed change r=1+tN²/K² gives exactly

    Y=(tN/K)² H_K,
    H_K=(1−d_−N²/(4K²))/(1+tN²/K²).

For unit K, H_K≡1 (mod p), so v_p(Y)=2v_p(N). In fact H_K is a
square in every Q_p with p|N, by odd-prime Hensel lifting. Thus this
removes the local Y obstruction, not just its parity symptom. It need not
be a square in Q. Positivity requires K²>d_−N²/4, equivalent here to
the stated interval; checking this and all units is still necessary. X's
local class remains 5R. Imposing H_K=h² explicitly leads to

    z²(4t h²+d_−)=4(1−h²),  z=N/K,

a bidegree-(2,2) genus-one equation on its smooth model, with only the
trivial z=0,h=±1 points immediately supplied. Its required nonzero rational
point, z's valuation and the X lift remain unpaid. This identifies the
exact remaining equation rather than declaring the original parity failure
an impossibility for all modifications.

**Other residues with the same trace do not fix this section.** For unit r,
b≡0 (mod N) implies r²≡1 (mod N). At each odd prime power dividing N,
r is +1 or −1: the two choices give (X,Y)≡(s,0) or (0,s).
Mixed signs can already be split using gcd(r−1,N). Hence simply replacing
the r≡1 residue by another trace-compatible one cannot remove a nonsquare-5
obstruction for P(r). A genuinely different residue drops the common-trace
condition and requires a new packet/reduction proof.

With t=cR, s≡(1+c²)R and a known rational a²=1+c², the circularity
statement is correct **if a is a modular unit**: any displayed-section
lift u²=X on r≡1 gives (u/a)²≡R. On r≡−1 use v/a instead. Require
c, c²−1 and a to be units, as well as all denominators; c²−1 handles
distinct modular roots. The explicit parametrization
c=2h/(1−h²), a=(1+h²)/(1−h²) makes a known without a root oracle,
but does not produce u. It removes the constant obstruction while making
the remaining lift already sufficient for the desired modular root. This
is a one-way reduction for prescribed unit witnesses, not a hardness proof.
Here **s=(1+c²)R must mean a modular coefficient condition** if the
quadratic-field mechanism is retained: literal rational equality makes
Delta=(c²−1)²R² a square and f split over Q. Taking a lift
s=(1+c²)R+N L can avoid that failure, but nonsquare Delta, positivity and
the required sum-of-two-squares anchor must be constructed and checked anew.
For this generalized nodal family the same argument gives lambda(P)=c²
using kappa=(c²−1)R; varying c here supplies p−1 bases, not good curves.

## 7. The distinct fixed-u curve — good reduction and a concrete escape

Fix u and D=f(u²)≠0. The different genus-one curve

    C_D: Z²=D(v⁴−s v²+t²)

has the explicit point (v,Z)=(u,D). Its branch polynomial is separable
when t Delta≠0. At p|N it has good reduction provided u is p-integral
and D is a p-unit: the branch points are ±sqrt(R),±2sqrt(R), four
distinct points. The square root of R is used only to describe the geometry;
it is not given to a solver. Nonunit D requires its own gcd/degeneracy branch.

One Jacobian model is

    J_D: eta²=xi(xi+D(s+2t))(xi+D(s−2t)).             (2)

This follows by twisting the even-quartic Jacobian by D; over sqrt(D) the
curve is Z'²=v⁴−s v²+t². Equivalently (2) is the standard two-isogenous
curve of eta²=xi(xi²−Ds xi+D²t²). Computing c4 and discriminant in (2)
gives 16D²(s²+12t²) and 256D⁶t²Delta², respectively, hence

    j(C_D)=16(s²+12t²)³/(t²Delta²)
           ≡4·73³/81 (mod p).                      (3)

The proposed invariant is correct. It is independent of D, u and any
lift of s retaining s≡5R. These reductions range through **at most two
quadratic twist classes**, and at most two elliptic group orders per p;
neither class is asserted to occur under the chosen u law. This remains
an upper bound at exceptional j. Among p∤30, j=0 only at p=73, and
j=1728 only at p=7,17, since

    j−1728=4(5·7·17)²/81.

All twists at these j number gcd(6,p−1) or gcd(4,p−1), respectively:
the coefficients in y²=x³+b and y²=x³+a x are classified modulo sixth
and fourth powers. But varying D here gives only quadratic twists, not all
of them. At p=7 those two even
coalesce (a quadratic twist of y²=x³+a x is isomorphic when p≡3 mod 4).
Thus a blanket statement of exactly two classes would be incorrect.

For t=cR, s≡(1+c²)R, the cross-ratio and invariant become

    ell=((c−1)/(c+1))²,
    j_c=16(c⁴+14c²+1)³/[c²(c²−1)⁴].                (4)

These require c(c²−1) to be a unit. Varying c can genuinely vary the
geometric curve; varying only the lift of s cannot do so modulo p.

**Concrete operation avoiding the two square searches:** keep u fixed and
perform group operations on C_D itself. Both X=u² and Y=v² are then
squares by construction; choose the new trace s_j=u²+v² afterward. Unlike
the norm quartic's four two-torsion points, the two sign points (u,±D)
generically have a difference of infinite order. Here is a symbolic proof
and an explicit lower-cost ECM interface. The degree-two map

    (v,Z)↦(U,V)=(v²/t, vZ/t)
    M_D: B V²=U³+A U²+U,
    A=−s/t,  B=1/(Dt)                              (5)

is well defined on the smooth completions. Its known image is
Q=(u²/t,uD/t). Over Q(u,sqrt(D)), scaling to the constant curve
Y²=x(x²−s x+t²) sends Q to (u²,u sqrt(D)). A torsion point on a
constant elliptic curve in characteristic zero has constant coordinates
over the algebraic closure of the constant field. Since u² is nonconstant,
Q is not torsion over Q(u). With (u,D) as origin on C_D, subtracting
Q from (5) makes it an isogeny; (u,−D) then maps to −2Q. This proves
the asserted generic infinite-order difference without a numerical example.
It does not certify every chosen rational u.

For packet use, the remaining condition is **u²+v²≡s (mod N)**,
besides distinct valid second field, actual ordinary field-square target
and valid denominators. The displayed seed has trace 2u² and need not
satisfy it. Group operations on C_D need not preserve it either. Selecting
u from the paid original sum-of-two-squares anchor supplies a point with
trace exactly s, but that is the coincident-field case. Producing a different
useful point with the prescribed trace still has no charged success law.
Thus this operation really removes a representation failure, while moving
the missing computation to an explicit congruence/field-square filter.
Rational candidate generation must pay its actual growing heights; the
generic-order proof supplies no input-specific height or useful-hit bound.

For ECM use, (5) bypasses that packet filter entirely. Its modular setup
uses polynomial bit work and its scalar M uses O(log M) modular group
operations at O(log N)-bit width, plus all gcds and curve retries. It is a
degree-two **isogenous quotient**, not a birational identification with (2);
its invariant is 256(s²−3t²)³/(t⁴Delta), generally different from (3).
The isogenous curves have the same order over each good finite field, so
this change supplies efficient arithmetic, not an independent order sample.

## 8. Primary ECM prior art and final scoped recommendation

In (5), the generalized modular coefficients give A=−(c+c⁻¹), exactly
Montgomery's full-two-torsion parameter A=k+k⁻¹ with k=−c. This forces
three rational two-torsion points on that modular curve; it does not force
Suyama's three-torsion or the extra four-torsion of B=A+2. For arbitrary
lifted s these stronger statements over Q cannot be inferred from reduction.

[Montgomery 1987, §§10.3.1–10.3.2, pp.260–263](https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/1987-48-177/S0025-5718-1987-0866113-7/S0025-5718-1987-0866113-7.pdf)
already gives point-bearing full-two-torsion curves, the A=k+k⁻¹ selection,
stronger torsion selections and x-coordinate arithmetic. His square-triple
construction also contains P itself: choose the three squares (2t)²,w²,s²
and translate x to remove the quadratic term. Thus neither having this
explicit point nor the variable-c full-two-torsion ECM mechanism is new
at that scope. This is not an asserted isomorphism to Suyama's family.

[Bernstein–Birkner–Lange–Peters, 2009-12-29, §7, pp.27–29](https://eecm.cr.yp.to/eecm-20091229.pdf)
provides explicit positive-rank families with larger torsion, including its
own Edwards translation, and discusses height growth. These are concrete
alternative point constructors if ordinary ECM is the intended operation.
Their existence gives no smooth-order or packet-lift law for this N,R stream.
[Barbulescu et al., 2012, introduction](https://arxiv.org/html/1202.4285v1#S1)
confirms that studying such parameter families and torsion divisibility is
an established ECM question; no theorem from its later sections is imported.

Recommend scoped acceptance of the birational identities, obvious subgroup,
generic infinite-order proof, genus-three description, exact local failure,
local repair and corrected good-quartic invariant/twist analysis. Narrow the
nonsquare-5 claim to its section/residue domain; use (1) for multiples.
The decisive remaining work is either a charged useful trace/field-square
filter on §7's rational points, or a specific ECM family selection claim
stronger than this known construction. No favorable point, congruence or
smooth-order distribution is established. No candidate was run. The saved
point/coordinate searches do not yet imply any end-to-end improvement.

Date: 2026-10-08. **PROVISIONAL parent derivation for independent review.**
Verified new complete factoring improvement: NONE. Symbolic work only.

## Computation being changed

The accepted W004 construction fixes both fields, then searches for a packet
which is twisted-square in the first and ordinary-square in the second.
Here construct the second trace from a rational square certificate. This
eliminates that second-field square test/search algebraically. The remaining
modular constraint is explicit below, and appears to retain the hard root
choice rather than solving it. This is a concrete generator, not a point oracle.

Take integers u,v,t with s=u^2+v^2, t=2R, s congruent to 5R modulo odd N,
and gcd(N,30R)=1. The first field is the accepted irreducible
f_1(T)=T^2-sT+t^2. Its packet is

    Q(T)=(t^2-u^2*T)*(v^2-T),
    Q(alpha_1)=alpha_1*(v^2-alpha_1)^2.

The blinded norm sampler now supplies the residue pair cheaply under its
strict interface; the first lifted u,v can be obtained by the accepted selector.
The formulas here also work for any such fixed first anchor.

Write d=v^2-u^2. Choose a nonzero rational parameter tau and put

    H=(tau+d/tau)/2,       k=(tau-d/tau)/2,
    h=t*H,                D=k^2-u^2,
    s_2=-(u^2*v^2+t^2+2*t*H*k)/D.                         (1)

Skip D=0. Since H^2-k^2=d, coefficient comparison modulo
f_2(T)=T^2-s_2*T+t^2 gives the exact identity

    Q(alpha_2)=(h+k*alpha_2)^2.                            (2)

Indeed the constant coefficients are t^2*(v^2-u^2), and the alpha_2
coefficients agree by the definition of s_2. This constructs an ordinary
square, with its root, in a field chosen afterward. Testing irreducibility of
f_2 and distinctness from the first quadratic field is still charged, and
failed choices remain failures. No positive supply is asserted for those tests.

s_2 is rational here. This deliberately changes W004's integral-trace selector.
Before modular use require tau and D to be units in Z_(N), so h,k,s_2 lie
in Z_(N). Every rational denominator is cleared and checked. One may work
with the rational quadratic algebra and the explicit root h+k*alpha_2;
there is no appeal to the old integral-root trace formula in this step.
Positivity s_2>2t is not claimed or needed by identities (1)-(2).
If some downstream construction requires it, that is a separate filter.

## The actual modular equation

Require s_2 congruent to s modulo N, ensuring f_2(R)=0.
Set g=v^2-R. For unit tau,D the trace condition is equivalent to

    (tau^2-R)*(9R*tau^2-d^2)=0 mod N.                     (3)

Exact derivation before reduction: writing F=-(u^2*v^2+t^2+2tHk),
one has
4*tau^2*(F-sD)=
 -(2t+s)*tau^4 +(2s^2-4u^2v^2-4t^2)*tau^2 +(2t-s)*d^2.
Using t=2R and s=5R modulo N factors this as the negative of (3).
No factorization of N is used in the identity.

When g is a unit, reduction of the explicit ordinary square root produces

    y=(h+kR)/g = R*(3tau^2+d)/(2*tau*g),    y^2=R mod N.  (4)

Thus a valid tau is already a root-producing certificate, and can be verified
in polynomial time. This alone is not an efficient method to find tau.

For a clean separated-branch analysis additionally require d, g, and
v^2-4R to be units. A proper gcd in those checks returns a factor; a full
gcd may be skipped. Their product restrictions are not granted positive mass.
Modulo each p^e dividing N the two factors of (3) cannot both be divisible by p,
because d^2-9R^2=4*(v^2-R)*(v^2-4R). Hence each local branch satisfies exactly

    tau^2=R,       giving y=tau,
    or 9R*tau^2=d^2, giving y=d/(3tau).                    (5)

If both types occur at different prime powers, gcd(tau^2-R,N) immediately
splits N. If the type is uniform globally, (5) still gives a root of R.
The four local parameter roots correspond to two choices of root sign and
two branch types. Repeated primes need the unit separation just stated.

## Why the easy construction from the outer x is not a speedup

Knowing x with x^2=R makes two global branches cheap:

    tau = x mod N,        or tau = d/(3x) mod N.

One may use any rational/integer lift having these residues and charged
height. Both choices give y=x in (4). Negating either gives y=-x.
Thus generating the compatible field from either globally chosen branch,
and recovering its displayed ordinary square, yields a trivial outer gcd.
Random integer lifts, choosing between these two branches, or negating them
does not change this conclusion. In an irreducible quadratic field the only
two roots of the nonzero Q(alpha_2) are +/- the displayed one, so another
exact square-root algorithm cannot repair this correlation.

This closes only those explicit constructions. It does not prove that all
possible field distributions, all mixtures, or other packets are useless.
It also illustrates why root-choice independence of the ORIGINAL norm
certificate does not license later use of x in the field selector: the
new trace is outside the accepted inner interface if constructed this way.

The independent-root or mixed-local-sign problem is therefore still present
in a concrete low-degree congruence. To improve it, one would need a different
computation that finds useful tau without tying all local signs to x, with
paid probability and work; simply renaming (3) an easy quartic is not one.

## Cost, falsifier, and constructive response

For inputs and tau of b bits, (1)-(4), denominator checks and quadratic
irreducibility/distinctness tests have polynomial bit cost. Searching tau,
unbounded lift heights, rejection and branch distribution are not included
for free. A scan is a real algorithm but has no improved coverage bound.

The cheapest decisive test is symbolic: expand (1)-(2), factor the trace
residual, verify (4)-(5), and inspect the strict root-choice dependence.
No numerical run is proposed until an actual new tau-generation mechanism
survives that gate.

The failed assumption is that constructing an ordinary square before choosing
the field automatically removes the modular-root constraint. It instead moves
that constraint to (3). A materially different next computation would keep
the field selector entirely inside the blinded-certificate interface and use
its uniform residue distribution for a priced sieve or a coupled computation
over many parameter values. Such a computation must specify its actual
products/updates and success law; none is granted by this note.
